vaccines.booster: Not recommended for most people (ICVP valid for life)
vaccines.notes: Certificate (ICVP) valid from 10 days after vaccination. Age 60+ is a precaution. YF-VAX is the only US-licensed vaccine.

vaccines.booster: Every 2 years if still at risk
Every 5 years if still at risk
vaccines.notes: 4 capsules, one every other day; one package billed.

vaccines.booster: Third dose ≥1 year after the series if exposure continues
vaccines.notes: Adults 18–65: second dose 7 to 28 days after the first.
After a bite, a vaccinated traveler needs 2 doses (days 0, 3) and no immune globulin; an unvaccinated one needs immune globulin plus 4 doses (days 0, 3, 7, 14).
Havrix 0 and 6–12 months, Vaqta 0 and 6–18 months; the second dose can follow the trip.
Twinrix standard 0, 1, 6 months; accelerated 0, 7, 21–30 days and 12 months.
Single oral dose ≥10 days before exposure; no food or drink 60 minutes before and after.
Vimkunya, single dose, age 12+; CDC gives no lead time.
Adults who completed the routine series: one lifetime booster before travel to areas with poliovirus circulating.

CDC adult schedule: "3-dose series Engerix-B, PreHevbrio, or Recombivax HB at 0, 1, 6 months (minimum intervals: dose 1 to dose 2 = 4 weeks; dose 2 to dose 3 = 8 weeks; dose 1 to dose 3 = 16 weeks)". Months counted as 30 days. CDC gives no protection date: ready_days_after_last is null.

CDC adult schedule: "2-dose series only applies when 2 doses of Heplisav-B are used at least 4 weeks apart" (age 18+ per cdc.gov/hepatitis-b/hcp/vaccine-administration, reviewed 2025-09-18). CDC gives no protection date: ready_days_after_last is null.

antimalarials.label: Primaquine 30 mg base (2 × 26.3 mg tablets); G6PD test required
Tafenoquine (Arakoda) 200 mg weekly; G6PD test required; no NADAC price published

antimalarials_note: Start: CDC gives 1–2 days (atovaquone-proguanil, doxycycline, primaquine), 1–2 weeks (chloroquine), ≥2 weeks (mefloquine); the engine uses the longer bound. Adult doses only.

hepB_source.note: The Yellow Book hepatitis B chapter is no longer listed (404 on 2026-10-24); schedules taken from the CDC adult immunization schedule notes. PreHevbrio is under a voluntary recall (CDC page): not offered by the tool.
